title: Anthropic says Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis; Stanford files rival human proof
dek: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to generate a Lean-formalized proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis; hours later Stanford posted an independent all-human draft.
body:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and the proof has been formalized in the Lean proof assistant into a document that spans more than 250,000 pages. Hours after that claim, researchers at Stanford released an independent draft that they say is an entirely human proof. Mathematicians and the wider community are now checking whether either proof is correct.

## Why it matters

The Riemann hypothesis is math’s best-known open problem and has been unresolved for 167 years; a valid proof would settle a central question about the distribution of prime numbers. The competing claims put AI-assisted and human-only methods in direct competition on one of mathematics’ highest-stakes questions, with implications for how proofs are produced, verified and credited.

If one or both proofs hold up, the result could reshape practices around formal verification,the process of encoding proofs in a proof assistant so a computer checks each logical step—because Anthropic reports a Lean formalization exceeding 250,000 pages. Verification at that scale will demand sustained effort from experts and tools.

## The details

- Levent Alpöge, an Anthropic mathematician, says he used Claude, Anthropic’s large language model, to produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. 
- Anthropic’s claimed proof is formalized in the Lean proof assistant and reportedly totals more than 250,000 pages.  
- Stanford researchers published an independent draft shortly after Anthropic’s announcement; Stanford describes its draft as an all-human proof.  
- Mathematicians are currently checking whether either the Claude-assisted proof or the Stanford draft is valid.
- It is not yet known which, if either, proof will be accepted by the mathematical community, how long verification will take, or what role Anthropic’s model played in the technical details of the formalization.

## What to watch

Follow verification work by independent mathematicians and teams that check Lean formalizations; acceptance will require community scrutiny and probably peer-reviewed publication. Watch for detailed explanations from Anthropic and Stanford about methods, the role of Claude in generating or checking steps, and any replication or independent formal-verification efforts.

Source: reporting by The Decoder.
